pharm: Oral highly selective RET kinase inhibitor; blocks RET fusions and activating RET mutations with limited off-target kinase inhibition
quick: <50 kg: 120 mg orally BID; >=50 kg: 160 mg orally BID
With or without food (with food if PPI needed)
Can cause fetal harm; use effective contraception
Do not breastfeed during and for 1 week after the last dose
No adjustment in mild-severe; not studied in ESRD
Reduce starting dose in severe (Child-Pugh C)
No specific interaction; limit due to liver effects
Liver tests, BP, ECG/QTc, bleeding, thyroid, lung symptoms
summary: Selpercatinib (Retevmo) is a highly selective oral RET kinase inhibitor for advanced or metastatic RET fusion-positive NSCLC and thyroid cancers, RET-mutant medullary thyroid cancer, and RET fusion-positive solid tumors. Confirm the RET alteration before starting. Adult dosing is weight-based (<50 kg: 120 mg twice daily; >=50 kg: 160 mg twice daily) until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Key risks are hepatotoxicity, hypertension, QT prolongation, hemorrhage, hypersensitivity, ILD/pneumonitis, tumor lysis, impaired wound healing, hypothyroidism, and embryo-fetal toxicity.
indications: Treatment of adults with locally advanced or metastatic RET fusion-positive NSCLC
Treatment of adults and children 12 years and older with advanced or metastatic RET-mutant medullary thyroid cancer
Treatment of adults and children 12 years and older with advanced or metastatic RET fusion-positive thyroid cancer
Treatment of adults with locally advanced or metastatic RET fusion-positive solid tumors

dosage.d: <50 kg: 120 mg orally twice daily. >=50 kg: 160 mg orally twice daily
dosage.n: Confirm RET fusion or RET mutation per indication before starting; continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity
dosage.t: Twice daily, with or without food

dosage.d: Step down by 40 mg per dose per level (e.g., 160 mg BID to 120 mg BID to 80 mg BID to 40 mg BID); discontinue if not tolerated at lowest level
dosage.n: Withhold, reduce, or permanently discontinue based on hepatotoxicity, hypertension, QT, hemorrhage, hypersensitivity, or ILD grade

dosage.d: <50 kg: 40 mg twice daily. >=50 kg: 80 mg twice daily
dosage.n: Reduce starting dose in severe hepatic impairment; monitor closely

admin: Take capsules by mouth twice daily, with or without food, at about the same times each day
Swallow capsules whole; do not crush, chew, or open
Confirm RET alteration (fusion or mutation per indication) with an FDA-approved test before starting
If a dose of an acid-reducing agent is needed, follow labeling (take selpercatinib with food when a proton pump inhibitor is required); separate H2 blockers and antacids by timing
Withhold for at least 7 days before elective surgery and for at least 2 weeks after major surgery until wounds heal
moa: Selpercatinib is a potent, highly selective inhibitor of rearranged during transfection (RET) kinase, including RET fusions, activating RET point mutations, and predicted resistance-relevant variants. It blocks RET autophosphorylation and downstream signaling through MAPK and PI3K/AKT pathways, inhibiting proliferation and survival of RET-driven tumor cells in lung and thyroid cancers while sparing most off-target kinases such as VEGFR2.

absolute: Known serious hypersensitivity to selpercatinib or any excipient
monitor: Liver tests (ALT, AST, bilirubin) for hepatotoxicity
ECG and electrolytes for QT prolongation
Bleeding signs, wound healing, and thyroid function
relative: History of QT prolongation or significant cardiac disease
Bleeding risk or recent surgery (impaired wound healing)
Concomitant strong CYP3A inhibitors or inducers

preg: Based on mechanism and animal findings, selpercatinib can cause fetal harm. Verify pregnancy status before starting in females of reproductive potential and advise effective contraception during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose.
lact: There are no data on selpercatinib in human milk or its effects on the infant or milk production. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 1 week after the final dose.
renal: No dose adjustment is recommended for mild, moderate, or severe renal impairment. Selpercatinib has not been studied in end-stage renal disease; use with caution and monitor closely.
hepatic: Reduce the starting dose in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C): <50 kg to 40 mg twice daily and >=50 kg to 80 mg twice daily. No change for mild to moderate impairment, but monitor liver tests closely. Withhold, reduce, or discontinue for treatment-emergent hepatotoxicity per labeling.

interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction is described; limit alcohol due to additive hepatic effects.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor liver tests, blood pressure, ECG (QTc) with electrolytes, CBC, thyroid function, and pulmonary symptoms; monitor for tumor lysis in high-burden disease.
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; take with food if a proton pump inhibitor must be co-administered.
major: Strong CYP3A inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin) - raise selpercatinib levels; avoid or reduce selpercatinib dose
Strong and moderate CYP3A inducers (e.g., rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St John's wort) - lower selpercatinib levels; avoid
QT-prolonging drugs - additive QT risk; avoid or monitor ECG closely
minor: CYP2C8 substrates (selpercatinib raises repaglinide exposure) - monitor and consider dose adjustment of the substrate
moderate: Proton pump inhibitors - reduce selpercatinib absorption under fasting conditions; take selpercatinib with food if PPI cannot be avoided
H2-receptor antagonists and antacids - separate dosing (give selpercatinib 2 hours before or 10 hours after H2 blocker; 2 hours before or after antacids)
Antihypertensives may need titration as selpercatinib raises blood pressure

emergency: Severe headache, chest pain, or neurologic symptoms (hypertensive crisis)
Syncope, palpitations, or irregular heartbeat (QT prolongation)
Fever with rash and joint pain (hypersensitivity)
New or worsening cough, dyspnea, or fever (pneumonitis/ILD)
rare: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis in pediatric patients

monitoring: Liver tests (ALT, AST, bilirubin) at baseline, every 2 weeks for the first 3 months, then monthly
Blood pressure at baseline, after 1 week, then monthly; treat new or worsening hypertension
ECG and electrolytes (potassium, magnesium, calcium) at baseline and periodically for QT prolongation
CBC, thyroid function, and signs of bleeding, hypersensitivity, tumor lysis, or ILD; pregnancy status before starting
counsel: Take twice daily with or without food; swallow capsules whole and do not double up after a missed dose or vomiting
Report yellowing of skin or eyes, dark urine, unusual bleeding or bruising, severe headache, chest pain, or swelling (liver, bleeding, or blood-pressure effects)
Seek care for fainting, palpitations, new cough, shortness of breath, or fever (heart rhythm or lung effects)
Tell your surgeon you take this drug; it must be stopped before surgery because it slows wound healing
Use effective contraception during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose; do not breastfeed; check with your team before new medicines or antacids
pk: Target inhibition from first doses; responses develop over weeks
Median Tmax about 2 hours after oral dosing
Steady state in about 7 days with twice-daily dosing
pearls: Confirm RET fusion (NSCLC, thyroid cancer, solid tumors) or RET mutation (medullary thyroid cancer) before starting; tumor-agnostic use still requires documented RET fusion
Weight-based twice-daily dosing (<50 kg: 120 mg; >=50 kg: 160 mg) with stepwise 40-mg reductions for toxicity
Hepatotoxicity is early and frequent; the every-2-weeks liver-test schedule for the first 3 months is essential
Hypertension and QT prolongation need active management: check BP early, correct electrolytes, and review QT drugs
Hold at least 7 days before elective surgery and 2 weeks after major surgery for wound-healing risk; hypersensitivity can include fever, rash, and arthralgia and needs steroids plus hold
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless the next dose is due within 6 hours; skip the missed dose and resume the regular schedule. Do not take two doses at once. If vomiting occurs after a dose, do not take an extra dose; take the next dose at the regular time.
overdose: There is no specific antidote for selpercatinib overdose. Manage with supportive care, including cardiac monitoring (ECG for QT prolongation), blood pressure control, liver tests, and observation for bleeding and hypersensitivity. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
